title: Tech Note: Understanding the ASIFONT.MAP File
author: Christopher Chapman

historical_commentary.text: This note explains how to hand-edit a plain-text font substitution lookup file (ASIFONT.MAP) so that Macintosh font names/FOND IDs map to equivalent Windows fonts when porting a 4D database between platforms; this entire mechanism is a relic of an era before Unicode-aware, cross-platform font handling and is obsolete, since modern 4D relies on standard OS font matching and TrueType/OpenType fonts rather than a manual Mac-FOND-to-Windows-font translation table.
related_updates: Modern operating systems and 4D versions use standard cross-platform font names and Unicode text handling instead of a manual ASIFONT.MAP substitution file
ResEdit and classic Mac OS FOND resources are long obsolete, having been replaced by modern font formats (TrueType/OpenType) with standardized naming
4D for Windows historically ran on Altura's Mac2Win emulation layer in this era, a compatibility approach no longer used in current 4D releases
